tema: Preliminarily evaluates whether hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) reduces oxy-inflammation biomarkers in patients with long COVID.
diseno: Preliminary series of 5 long COVID subjects (athletes and patients with comorbidities) treated with 100% O2 at 2.4 ATA, 90 min, in different session protocols; saliva and/or urine biomarkers before and after treatment.
hallazgos: After treatment, ROS production, lipid peroxidation, DNA damage, NO metabolites and inflammation biomarkers were attenuated, especially in the athletes.
conclusion: HBOT could be considered a possible treatment for long COVID; larger samples are required, which could include other post-viral syndromes.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on oxy-inflammation and HBOT; the study does not specifically address ME/CFS and the sample description in the abstract is internally inconsistent (two or three athletes). The conclusions are cautious ('preliminary').

tema: Investigates the presence of antipituitary (APA) and antihypothalamus (AHA) antibodies and the associated hormonal dysfunctions in ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study (Stanford and Naples): 30 women with ME/CFS (Fukuda, Canadian and IOM criteria) and 25 age-matched healthy controls; detection of APA and AHA by immunofluorescence and study of anterior pituitary hormones and target glands.
hallazgos: Patients showed a high prevalence of AHA (33%) and APA (56%) and significantly lower levels of ACTH/cortisol and peak GH/IGF-1 than controls. The 13 patients with high titres (≥1:32) had lower hormone values and more severe forms of ME/CFS than those with low or negative titres.
conclusion: AHA and/or APA at high titres are associated with hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, suggesting that hypothalamic-pituitary autoimmunity may play an important role, especially in severe forms.
triangulacion: The conclusions come from the abstract itself, so they agree fully; the keywords (antipituitary antibodies, GH, IGF-1) reinforce the same neuroendocrine-autoimmune focus. There is no independent source for comparison.

tema: Investigates whether hypothalamic volumes differ in adolescents with ME/CFS and whether they are associated with fatigue severity and disease duration.
diseno: Volumetric study with T1 MRI in 48 adolescents (25 with ME/CFS and 23 controls); hypothalamic subregions and Bayesian linear and quantile regression models.
hallazgos: There was no evidence of volume differences between groups. In ME/CFS a weak relationship was found between right anterior-superior volume and fatigue, and a probable positive association between disease duration and right superior tubular volume.
conclusion: Hypothalamic volumes appear comparable in adolescence, but there are indications of paraventricular nucleus involvement; longitudinal replication in larger samples is required.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent and cautious; there is a discrepancy: the abstract describes the relationship with fatigue as an increase in volume and the conclusions call it a negative linear relationship with the total score.

tema: Proposes that astrocytic dysregulation of the sympathetic nervous system (SNS) causes metabolic dysfunction in a subgroup of patients with long COVID and ME/CFS.
diseno: Hypothesis article by an independent researcher, published in a journal of patient-generated hypotheses; no own empirical data.
hallazgos: Suggests that a noradrenergic genetic predisposition or astrocyte dysfunction (including that of β2-adrenergic receptors and SARS-CoV-2 infection) could overactivate the SNS and alter immunity, energy metabolism, sleep, breathing, gastrointestinal function and blood pressure, explaining fatigue, cognitive dysfunction and POTS symptoms.
conclusion: Research is needed to test these hypotheses to understand the mechanisms of long COVID and ME/CFS.
triangulacion: There are no keywords; the abstract is opening text and the conclusions come from the discussion. Both texts are consistent on the SNS-astrocyte axis; the discussion broadens toward GLUT4, β2AR and POTS.

tema: Proposes that rising serum soluble CD40 ligand (sCD40L) could be a biomarker of progression in ME/CFS and long COVID.
diseno: Hypothesis article by an independent patient-researcher (Patient-Generated Hypotheses Journal), based on a literature review; no own data.
hallazgos: Gathers studies indicating that sCD40L tends to rise progressively in ME/CFS, long COVID and multiple sclerosis. Its platelet origin would fit with findings of platelet activation (P-selectin, platelet-leukocyte aggregates) and it has been linked to endothelial activation, cell danger signalling, B immunity and neurocognitive impairment.
conclusion: sCD40L would be an accessible longitudinal measure and potentially useful as a progression biomarker, although it is not specific to ME/CFS or long COVID and studies must be designed accordingly.
triangulacion: There are no keywords, and the abstract is the opening text of the document; abstract and discussion are consistent on sCD40L as a longitudinal biomarker. The discussion adds an explicit warning about its lack of specificity.

tema: Suggests that symptomatic myodesopsia (vitreous floaters) could be a risk factor for long COVID and ME/CFS.
diseno: Hypothesis article from the Patient Led Research Collaborative based on literature and anonymous accounts from online communities; no systematic own data.
hallazgos: It is argued that myodesopsia could reflect susceptibility to collagen degradation in the face of inflammatory triggers, supported by collagen-degrading enzymes in the vitreous, associations with connective tissue disorders and with infections by various pathogens.
conclusion: They propose a prospective longitudinal study with a diagnostic definition combining symptoms and objective indicators; if confirmed, a simple eye screening could identify a higher-risk subgroup and guide genetic studies.
triangulacion: Keywords are missing; abstract and discussion are consistent on the collagen hypothesis. The discussion provides the method to test it and contains web page noise; the evidence cited is indirect.

tema: Identifies CD8 T lymphocyte dysfunction associated with symptoms in ME/CFS and long COVID and describes a retrospective series treated with a nebulized antioxidant/antipathogen agent.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with CD8 functional assay by intracellular cytokine staining in ME/CFS (n = 12), long COVID (n = 8) and healthy controls (n = 10), symptom questionnaires, plus a retrospective case series of nebulized treatment with five components.
hallazgos: CD8 T lymphocytes from both patient groups had a significantly lower capacity to produce IFNγ and TNFα after PMA stimulation, a feature reminiscent of clonal exhaustion associated with oxidative stress. Both disorders showed similar symptom profiles; in the case series immune dysfunction and health improved in parallel with the treatment.
conclusion: CD8 dysfunction could be a useful biomarker and the nebulized antioxidant/antipathogen treatment shows potential benefit, although this is a small study.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (taken from the abstract) are consistent on CD8 dysfunction and exhaustion and oxidative stress. The conclusions acknowledge the small sample size; the therapeutic evidence comes from an uncontrolled retrospective series.

tema: Study protocol that looks for altered biological factors and evaluates personalized lifestyle interventions for chronic fatigue in adolescents and young adults with QFS, ME/CFS and JIA.
diseno: RCT protocol with a single-subject (N=1) experimental case series design using experience sampling methodology, in young people aged 12-29 with QFS, ME/CFS and JIA; biological assessments of blood, stool, saliva and hair; comparison of personalized PROfeel lifestyle advice versus generic dietary advice. Registration NL8789.
hallazgos: Not applicable: it is a protocol without results; it describes the design and anticipates practical problems that can be solved through innovative design, statistical approaches and recruitment strategies.
conclusion: The study aims to contribute to biological research and personalized treatment of QFS and similar manifestations of chronic fatigue.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree on chronic fatigue, lifestyle advice and the biopsychosocial model; the conclusions (from the discussion) are only administrative noise (ethics, consent, affiliations). Its fit in the genetic/omic topic is weak, limited to the biological assessments.

tema: Analyses whether IgG responses against EBV peptides allow ME/CFS to be diagnosed and trigger autoimmunity through molecular mimicry.
diseno: Analysis of a large public dataset of IgG against 3054 EBV peptides in ME/CFS patients and healthy controls; super learner algorithm with training and test split (85% accuracy target) and bioinformatic analysis of homology with human proteins.
hallazgos: No effective classifier was found for all patients nor for those with a non-infectious or unknown trigger. A classifier of 26 antibodies distinguished patients with an infectious trigger from controls with 100% accuracy (training) and 90% (test); their importance did not correlate with homology to human proteins.
conclusion: These 26 antibodies have diagnostic potential in a subgroup, but their peptides probably do not induce autoimmune B responses; the role of EBV in autoimmunity should be reconsidered in light of danger theory.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on EBV, IgG and diagnosis. The keywords highlight molecular mimicry and autoimmunity, which the results do not support; the PDF conclusions add the reinterpretation from danger theory.

tema: Analyses the processes of subjectivity construction in people with fibromyalgia, CFS/ME and multiple chemical sensitivity as contested illnesses.
diseno: Exploratory qualitative study (hermeneutic phenomenology and ethnosociology) with life histories of 13 informants and sociological discourse analysis.
hallazgos: Three categories: self and grief; images and practices about the illnesses; relationships with health professionals; everyday experience is marked by stigmatization and exclusion.
conclusion: Nursing must reduce vulnerability and exclusion through empowerment, accompaniment, prevention of delegitimization and clinical spaces free of scepticism.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent around contested illness and stigma; the conclusions add the assertive position of the patient and the transformative role of professionals.

tema: Explores how the cytokines that discriminate ME/CFS change according to disease duration to improve biomarker validation.
diseno: Analysis of resting cytokine data from several studies in women with ME/CFS: ≤18 years and ≤2 years of illness (n = 18), 18-50 years with 7 years (n = 22) and ≥50 years with a mean of 11 years (n = 28), with age- and BMI-matched controls; 16 cytokines by chemiluminescence and linear classification models.
hallazgos: The optimal subselections included IL-1α, 6, 8, 15 and TNFα; IL-1α, 6 and 8 as a duration-adjusted triple screen achieved accuracies of 75-88%. The contribution of IL-1α decreased with duration, and IL-8 and IL-6 reversed their discriminating direction between recent illness and illness of more than 2 years.
conclusion: IL-1α, 6 and 8 adjusted for duration could serve as robust age-independent biomarkers, although clinical translation would be premature; disease progression can mask marker validation.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on cytokines, disease duration and biomarkers; the PDF conclusions are more cautious than the abstract in calling clinical application premature (with noise from supplementary files).

tema: Compares cytokine profiles and immune networks in cerebrospinal fluid between ME/CFS patients with classic and atypical presentation.
diseno: Cross-sectional study of CSF from 32 classic and 27 atypical ME/CFS cases with a 51-cytokine assay; logistic regression with variable selection and network analysis.
hallazgos: The atypical cases differed in cytokine profile, with a strong association with lower levels of IL-17A and CXCL9 in CSF, absence of inverse relationships between cytokines and sparser positive correlations. In the classic cases, the IL-1 receptor antagonist appeared to be a negative regulator, with patterns suggestive of altered IL-1 signalling and autoimmune-type activation.
conclusion: The CNS immune signatures in atypical patients may be distinct from the classic ones, which suggests exploring alternative non-immune mechanisms, exposure histories and longitudinal surveillance of comorbidities in this subgroup.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (from the discussion, with noise from legends and acknowledgements) are consistent on CSF, IL-17A and CXCL9; the conclusions go further in proposing non-immune mechanisms in the atypical cases.

tema: Evaluates immunoadsorption (IA) to remove autoantibodies against the β2-adrenergic receptor in patients with post-infectious CFS/ME.
diseno: Open pilot trial in 10 patients with post-infectious CFS/ME and elevated β2 autoantibodies, treated with IA with an IgG-binding column over 5 days; symptom scales, ELISA and B lymphocyte flow cytometry.
hallazgos: IgG fell to a median of 0.73 g/l after the 4th cycle and β2 antibodies decreased in 9 of 10 patients, remaining lower at 6 months. Memory B cells decreased and plasma cells increased. Seven patients improved rapidly; three maintained moderate-marked improvement for 6-12+ months.
conclusion: IA can remove anti-β2 autoantibodies and produce clinical improvement, with an effect on memory B cell development; the pilot study justifies further research.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions reproduce those of the abstract and add the introduction with the rituximab background and the antibodies against M3/M4 receptors. The keywords reflect the autoimmune and B cell focus well.

tema: Reanalyses intravenous immunoglobulin G (IV IgG) trials in ME/CFS to reassess its therapeutic value.
diseno: Detailed review of previous controlled trials and clinical observations in severe ME/CFS.
hallazgos: IgG would be very effective in a proportion of patients with severe, well-characterized ME/CFS, with responders predictable by markers of cellular immune dysfunction; transient exacerbation also occurred with placebo; headache was more frequent with IgG.
conclusion: They advocate reviving research and consider it justified to offer IgG to selected severe patients, with possible relevance in post-SARS-CoV-2 cases.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions are more emphatic (they call it 'potentially curative') but qualify that it only benefits a proportion of patients.

tema: Studies the relationship between immunological characteristics and intestinal barrier function in ME/CFS by stratifying patients by immune competence.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with ME/CFS patients divided into two groups (with and without immunodeficiency); ELISA measurement of inflammatory mediators and biomarkers of intestinal barrier integrity. Sample size not stated (cohorts described as small).
hallazgos: Immunodeficient patients showed reduced C4a levels, suggesting subgroup-specific dysregulation of innate immunity. Patients without immunodeficiency showed mucosal barrier leakage, with elevated LBP.
conclusion: Stratifying by immune competence distinguishes subgroups with distinct pathophysiological patterns, which is important for defining treatments; larger cohorts and standardized methods are needed.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent (stratification, C4a, intestinal barrier). The PDF conclusions are more cautious than the abstract: they acknowledge small cohorts, non-significant results that only indicate a trend and doubt about whether the C4a deficit is cause or consequence.

tema: Looks for an ME/CFS-specific serum immunosignature using random-sequence peptide microarrays.
diseno: Case-control study with ME/CFS sera according to Canadian criteria: Canadian cohort (25 cases and 25 controls), 25 cases from Norwegian phase 1/2 trials and 6 US healthy controls; unsupervised and supervised analyses.
hallazgos: A candidate immunosignature of 654 peptides differentiated ME/CFS from controls in the Canadian cohort; refined with the Norwegian and US samples, it ended up as a 256-peptide signature that separated cases and controls in the international sets.
conclusion: Despite the small sample size, the 256-peptide signature clearly separates ME/CFS from controls and suggests that the 'hit-and-run' hypothesis of immune dysfunction deserves further research in larger cohorts.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion agree on serum antibodies as a diagnostic biomarker. The discussion adds the limitation of sample size and the possibility of longitudinal studies; it contains noise from acknowledgements and licence text.

tema: Evaluates the effect of life stressors (work, income, family situation) on symptom severity in an Australian ME/CFS cohort.
diseno: 5-month longitudinal study with questionnaires in 36 patients (age 41.25 ± 12.14; response rate 83.7%).
hallazgos: Symptoms fluctuated; sleep disturbances tended to be severe; work and income were associated with worse cognitive, gastrointestinal, pain and sleep symptoms; greater access to services was associated with better symptoms.
conclusion: Work and financial stressors can exacerbate symptoms; stress mitigation and support for patients who cannot work are stressed.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions add the reduction in full-time employment and the financial instability of the cohort.

tema: Evaluates the impact of prolonged cryopreservation on immune markers in blood of ME/CFS patients for biomarker discovery.
diseno: Comparative flow cytometry immunophenotyping study in fresh blood and frozen PBMC from ME/CFS patients (n = 18) and matched healthy controls (n = 18), with a cytokine production assay after stimulation.
hallazgos: Markers of Treg subpopulations, CD56 expression on T lymphocytes, the frequency of effector CD8 and CD57 on NK cells were not altered. In contrast, CD25 and CD69 on NK cells increased and NKp46 was markedly reduced after cryopreservation; in biobanked PBMC there were no differences between patients and controls.
conclusion: Some T and NK lymphocyte markers become unstable after cryopreservation, which limits their use in studies with biobanked samples and calls for new tools to assess their stability.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent (cryopreservation, NK, NKp46). The conclusions text corresponds to acknowledgements and supplementary figures, so it provides no conclusions of its own.

tema: Reviews how drugs affect mitochondrial function and the opportunities to repurpose them as treatments, with a focus on cancer and immunomodulation.
diseno: Narrative literature review on drug-induced mitochondrial toxicity and mitochondria-modulating agents. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Many drug classes (antidiabetics, antibiotics, chemotherapeutics, antivirals) affect the mitochondria through mtDNA depletion, increased ROS and OXPHOS uncoupling, as off-target effects; some are being explored for repositioning in cancer, the immune system and neurodegenerative diseases.
conclusion: Drugs with mitochondrial effects represent a growing therapeutic opportunity, although the great challenge is selectivity to preserve mitochondrial function in healthy tissues.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent. None of the sources mentions ME/CFS; its relationship to the topic is indirect (mitochondrial dysfunction and chronic viral infection).

tema: Measures TRPM3-dependent calcium influx in NK cells from ME/CFS patients and its restoration with naltrexone in vitro.
diseno: In vitro experimental study with NK cells isolated from 10 ME/CFS patients and 10 age- and sex-matched controls; live-cell immunofluorescence imaging with a TRPM3 agonist (pregnenolone sulphate) and antagonist (ononetin) and naltrexone treatment for 24 h.
hallazgos: At baseline, the amplitude and mean time of the Ca2+ response were significantly reduced in patients' NK cells (p < 0.0001). After naltrexone, the mean time did not differ from controls and the amplitude increased significantly.
conclusion: Loss of TRPM3 function alters Ca2+ influx, which supports ME/CFS being a TRP channelopathy, and naltrexone is a possible therapeutic intervention.
triangulacion: The three sources are fully consistent on TRPM3, calcium, NK and naltrexone. The PDF conclusions are somewhat more cautious, speaking of 'additional evidence' of the potential benefit without repeating the claim of TRP channelopathy.

tema: Explores in vitro the response of B cells from ME/CFS patients to rapid changes in energy demand and the role of CD24, CD38 and metabolism.
diseno: In vitro experimental study with B cells from ME/CFS patients and healthy controls, stimulated via the B cell receptor with T-dependent or TLR9 costimulation; immunophenotype (CD24, CD38, CD39, CD73, mitochondrial mass) and metabolomics by 1H-NMR. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Proliferating B cells from ME/CFS showed lower mitochondrial mass, greater consumption of essential amino acids, delayed loss of CD24 and higher CD38 expression after stimulation.
conclusion: The results suggest a stress response in ME/CFS B cells with use of additional substrates to maintain ATP, confirming alterations of energy metabolism in a dynamic model.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent. The available conclusions text is only noise (contributions, funding), so the conclusion is based on the abstract's discussion.

tema: Evaluates circulating biomarkers of intestinal barrier dysfunction and bacterial translocation in fibromyalgia (FM) and ME/CFS and their association with symptoms.
diseno: Multicentre cross-sectional pilot study with 22 FM patients, 30 with ME/CFS and 26 matched controls; ELISA of anti-β-LGB, ZO-1, LPS, sCD14 and IL-1β, validated questionnaires (SF-36, COMPASS-31) and ROC curves.
hallazgos: Anti-β-LGB, ZO-1, LPS and sCD14 were elevated in FM and in ME/CFS compared with controls (more so in FM), with no differences in IL-1β. In ME/CFS, ZO-1 correlated with COMPASS-31; the four markers discriminated patients from controls well.
conclusion: Intestinal barrier and inflammation biomarkers are associated with autonomic dysfunction and could predict barrier dysfunction, although studies on their causality are required before clinical application.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent on intestinal permeability, bacterial translocation and LPS. The conclusions text is only supplementary figure legends, so it provides no additional information.

tema: Explores the association between burns and the subsequent risk of CFS.
diseno: Population-based retrospective cohort (Taiwan national health insurance): 17,204 patients with newly diagnosed burns matched 1:4 for age, sex, year and comorbidities with the general population; Cox regression.
hallazgos: The incidence of CFS was 1.61 versus 0.86 per 1000 person-years (adjusted HR 1.48; 95% CI 1.41-1.56), with higher risk in all stratifications. Burns in sun-exposed areas (face and limbs), extensive burns and visible scars were associated with greater impact.
conclusion: Thermal injury is associated with a higher risk of CFS; patients and physicians should be aware of this risk and consider preventive measures to promote recovery.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The PDF conclusions are brief and focus on clinical implications, without taking up the nuances on location and scars in the abstract; the keywords are generic.

tema: Clarifies the risk of CFS after the diagnosis of psoriasis, an immune-based dermatological disease.
diseno: Population-based retrospective cohort (Taiwan): 2616 patients ≥20 years with psoriasis diagnosed in 2004-2008 and 10,464 without psoriasis, followed until 2011; Cox regression.
hallazgos: The incidence of CFS was 3.58 versus 2.27 per 1000 person-years (adjusted HR 1.48; 95% CI 1.07-2.06), with higher risk in men (HR 2.05) and in those ≥60 years (HR 2.32). The risk was attenuated in those who received phototherapy or immunomodulators.
conclusion: Psoriasis significantly increases the risk of CFS, especially in men and older people, and this risk can be attenuated with phototherapy or immunomodulatory drugs.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the keywords include phototherapy, immunomodulators and sex differences. The PDF conclusions highlight the attenuation by treatment, which the abstract's conclusion does not mention.

tema: Reviews how systemic inflammation of peripheral organs causes neuroinflammation, with attention to susceptible brain regions.
diseno: Narrative review of studies on peripheral inflammation (gastrointestinal, COPD, rheumatoid arthritis, dermatitis, CFS/ME) and neuroinflammation.
hallazgos: The mechanisms described are disruption of the blood-brain barrier, glial activation associated with systemic immune activation and effects on autonomic nerves through the organ-brain axis.
conclusion: It is difficult to compare neuroinflammation between diseases because of the heterogeneity of assessments and of degrees of systemic inflammation; morphological studies with homogeneous inflammatory criteria in various peripheral diseases are needed.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent on the blood-brain barrier, glia and autonomic nerves. The discussion focuses on methodological limitations (with repeated sentences and funding noise) and ME/CFS appears only as one example among several diseases.
